alt: A grid comparing Taylorism, Fordism and post-Fordism by source, key features and sociological reading, with a note that the Luddites opposed how machines were used rather than machines themselves.

alt: Three sectors of work: extraction, with the mining community of Coal Is Our Life; manufacturing, with factory discipline; and services, with Hochschild’s emotional labour. A note frames the deskilling debate.
caption: Each sector shaped community, control and emotion at work differently.

alt: Railways, cars and air travel compared: Schivelbusch on rail perception and standard time, the Model T, car-based cities that disadvantage people without cars, and unevenly shared air travel, with environmental effects.
caption: Each transport revolution brought freedom for some and costs for many.

alt: Four explanations of consumption: Veblen’s display, Bourdieu’s taste and cultural capital, Baudrillard’s sign value and planned obsolescence such as the Phoebus cartel, with evaluation.

after: ## Technological determinism versus social construction: further cases
alt: A spectrum from determinist cases (White’s stirrup, Marx, McLuhan) through middle positions (Latour, soft determinism) to constructionist cases (Winner, Cowan, Wajcman). A diagram shows the two reasons household machines did not reduce women’s housework time.
